hero.filename: Photograph of Gurdwara Janam Asthan in Nankana Sahib, 1935.jpg
hero.title: File:Photograph of Gurdwara Janam Asthan in Nankana Sahib, 1935.jpg
hero.source: Photograph of Gurdwara Janam Asthan in Nankana Sahib, 1935
hero.description:
Photograph of Gurdwara Janam Asthan [alt. known as 'Gurdwara Nankana Sahib'] in Nankana Sahib, 1935. 
The Janam Asthan [sacred birthplace that is marked by the main shrine], Shahid Ganj [place of martyrdom], and Shahidi Jand [martyrs' tree], from which many Sikhs were tied upside-down and were burnt-alive during the Nankana massacre [alt. known as 'Saka Nankana'] of 1921, are visible.

gallery.filename: Charred remains of Sikhs murdered in the Nankana massacre (Saka Nankana) of 1921.jpg
gallery.title: File:Charred remains of Sikhs murdered in the Nankana massacre (Saka Nankana) of 1921.jpg
gallery.source: Charred remains of Sikhs murdered in the Nankana massacre (Saka Nankana) of 1921
gallery.description:
Charred remains of Sikhs murdered in the Nankana massacre (Saka Nankana) of 1921. These Sikh martyrs were burnt alive by Mahant Narain Das when they marched towards Nankana Sahib to free the gurdwara from the mahant's control.
An image of this photograph can also be found at: [1]

Photograph of the mass funeral of Sikh martyrs of the Nankana massacre ('Saka Nankana'). The charred and incinerated remains of the Sikh victims are visible in-frame.
